values: Manager view: the next two months cover product launch validation, security, performance, architecture, observability and AWS deployment automation. The work is sequenced by risk and can run in parallel where ownership is clear.
Moving from feature delivery toward a production-ready product rollout.
Full API testing plus 3 load-testing rounds: baseline, peak traffic, and sustained-use/recovery.
Frontend, backend, APIs, database migrations, security, performance, observability and AWS deployment automation.
High-risk architecture and performance work stays with Prasath; scoped execution can be delegated to Sai Varshini.
Why it matters to the product
Turn the current engineering work into a controlled product launch with clear go/no-go decisions.
Release checklist; environment readiness; rollback plan; ownership and escalation matrix.
Prepare evidence pack, checklist formatting and follow-up tracking.
All workstreams feed into this gate.
Approved launch checklist and rollback decision record.
Full API functional and regression testing
Confirm that existing and newly changed APIs work together across user journeys before release.
Complete API inventory; positive/negative test cases; regression report; defects triaged by severity.
Execute assigned test cases, record evidence and retest fixes.
No unresolved critical or high-severity API defects.
Measure current response time, throughput and resource usage before tuning the system.
Baseline report covering all APIs; bottleneck list; agreed performance thresholds.
Prepare test data, run repeatable scripts and document results.
API inventory and representative test data.
Baseline metrics and prioritized bottleneck list.
Test whether the platform can handle expected production concurrency and traffic spikes.
Peak-load test report; capacity limits; tuning actions; evidence of system behavior under stress.
Support execution, monitor test runs and capture failure evidence.
Peak scenario passes agreed thresholds or has a documented capacity plan.
Load testing round 3: soak and failure recovery
Check stability over sustained usage and confirm the platform recovers from slowdowns or dependency failures.
Soak test; restart/recovery checks; timeout and retry evidence; final performance sign-off.
Run repeat checks and maintain the failure/recovery evidence log.
No unacceptable memory, queue, timeout or recovery issues.
Verify that sensitive data is protected in transit, at rest and through access-controlled flows.
Encryption configuration review; transport-security checks; storage/access validation; findings and remediation log.
Collect configuration evidence and track remediation items.
Environment access and security test accounts.
Security findings are closed, accepted or formally risk-owned.
Separate the volume functionality so it can be deployed, tested and scaled without destabilizing unrelated product areas.
Service boundary; isolated routes/models/storage adapters; independent test coverage; deployment notes.
Own targeted regression cases and documentation for the isolated boundary.
API regression coverage and database/storage decisions.
Volume flows can be tested and released independently.
Make schema changes safer for production by validating ordering, rollback and compatibility with existing code.
Migration inventory; forward-run and rollback tests; backup/restore check; release sequencing.
Primary execution owner with Prasath review for high-risk changes.
Stable staging database and release branch.
Migrations run predictably with a tested rollback path.
Reduce future defect risk and make the codebase easier for the team to review, support and extend.
Readability pass on high-change modules; duplication cleanup; naming/documentation improvements; review checklist.
Primary owner for scoped cleanup and documentation; escalate architecture changes.
Focus on modules touched by rollout work.
Reviewed cleanup changes with no behavior regression.
Prepare the frontend for independent ownership and deployment as the product grows.
Boundary proposal; shared-component rules; deployment/versioning approach; migration sequence for priority screens.
Document current dependencies and identify candidate modules for later separation.
Frontend dependency map and release constraints.
Approved scaling design and prioritized migration backlog.
Restructure high-change backend areas so they can scale and be maintained independently instead of growing as one tightly coupled system.
Service-boundary assessment; API contract cleanup; dependency map; phased re-engineering plan.
Support API inventory, contract documentation and low-risk refactoring tasks.
Volume isolation findings and load-test bottlenecks.
Architecture decision record and sequenced implementation plan.
Improve response times and reduce repeated database work for frequently requested data.
Cache candidate list; invalidation rules; stale-data policy; performance comparison before/after.
Implement or test scoped cache candidates after rules are approved.
Load-test evidence and data freshness requirements.
Measured improvement with no unacceptable stale-data behavior.
Move long-running or retryable work out of user-facing requests so the product stays responsive and resilient.
Queue candidate list; retry/dead-letter rules; idempotency checks; monitoring and operational runbook.
Document candidate workflows and test consumer behavior for assigned queues.
Service boundaries, failure scenarios and monitoring.
Priority workflows have an approved queue design and implementation backlog.
Give the team a live view of product health so issues can be detected before users report them.
Grafana dashboards for API latency, error rate, availability, database/cache/queue health and AWS resource usage; alert thresholds; on-call/runbook notes.
Support dashboard QA, alert testing and evidence capture for assigned services.
Application logs/metrics, AWS access and load-test scenarios.
Dashboards and alerts are live, tested and linked to an incident response runbook.
AWS serverless deployment pipeline using SAM
Make deployments repeatable and safer across development, staging and production instead of relying on manual configuration.
AWS SAM templates; parameterized environments; IAM/secrets configuration; CI/CD pipeline; deployment, rollback and smoke-test steps.
Maintain environment inventory, execute smoke tests and document deployment evidence.
AWS account permissions, secrets, build artifacts and rollback approval.
A SAM-based pipeline can deploy and roll back a tested release with an auditable result.
Recording API upload capacity and size limits
Increase the current recording upload limit so real product files can be submitted reliably without failed or truncated uploads.

Raise the configured upload limit across the API gateway/serverless runtime/application/storage path; test large files; document timeout, memory and retry behavior; use multipart or chunked upload if a single request remains too small.
Run large-file regression tests, capture failure evidence and update the upload support notes.
API gateway/request limits, Lambda/runtime limits, storage configuration, network timeout and retry settings.
Large recording uploads complete end-to-end within the documented limit, with a tested fallback for larger files.
